author: ajkerrigan
body:
This is partly addressing #7116 , and partly me figuring out the flow of adding Azure resources. High-level:

- Add the package dependency we need to manage Defender (Security Center) resources
- Add resource types under the Defender umbrella
  - The SDK breaks these out into separate resource types (pricing, settings, auto-provisioning settings...). We may want to reorganize them, but for a first pass I tried to follow existing conventions.

The client creation for Defender resources looked different from any other Azure service client examples I saw. I'm not sure how much this is "Defender is different" and how much is "I haven't looked at enough Azure stuff". I stole the Azure CLI's approach though - it was much simpler than my first attempt.

author: maurizi
body:
## Overview

The PlanScore backend has a file size limitation for direct upload, but allows any size file if you instead upload your file directly to S3 using a signed URL as part of a multi-step API.

Updating our app to make use of this more complex API made things quite a bit more complex, and also a bit more robust:
 - Our check for whether its safe to call the PlanScore API wasn't quite right (there can be unassigned areas, but every districts needs something assigned to it)
 - We weren't making use of their ability to poll for when the report is complete - previously we made the link available even when PlanScore wasn't done processing it.

### Checklist

- [x] Description of PR is in an appropriate section of `CHANGELOG.md` and grouped with similar changes, if possible

### Demo

![send-to-planscore](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4432106/155221495-a65e68fe-ba00-4a6a-8708-6838d6614f62.gif)


### Notes

I initially attempted to do this in a "stateless" fashion, hitting our backend for API requests to PlanScore but posting to S3 directly from the browser, which would have eliminated the need to do polling on the client.

Unfortunately I couldn't get this to work, due to both CORS issues and complications with using the callback approach for the S3 upload.

## Testing Instructions

- `scripts/update`
- If you don't already have it configured, contact @maurizi for the DistrictBuilder PlanScore token, then add it to your `.env` file
- On a map with some districts assigned, go to the Evaluate page, and then the competitiveness detail. You should see a "Send to PlanScore" button.
  - If any of your districts don't have any area assigned to them yet, it should be disabled
  - Once enabled, clicking it should move the button to a loading state
  - Loading will take... a while... but should eventually finish (if it doesn't, you should eventually see an error once it times out)
  - Once done loading, the "View on PlanScore" link should take you directly to the completed report
- If you refresh the page, the "View on PlanScore" link should still be present. If you make some changes and save, it should switch back to "Send to PlanScore"

Closes #1131

author: kuujo
body:
This PR defaults logger names to the caller's package name when no name is specified.

```go
var logger = logging.GetLogger()
```

The standard syntax for creating loggers will use fully qualified name of the package in which the logger is created. This creates a good default for logger names that can be implemented by simply removing the existing names from the loggers in all code.

body:
This re-introduce the full hash and compre functions for Address,
which was reverted https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/1d30fc5cb64ecba2f03fe42aa0d8c65c3decad82 (https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/17851).

The issue https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/17831, which is fixed by https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/17851, is handled in a different way;
simply ignore to configure the conflicted DHCPv6 address. Previously, we
warn about the conflict, but continue to configure the address anyway, and
the kernel ignores the request. So, it is not necessary to request the
conflicted address in networkd side.

This fixes the following issues:
- when a link has an address, and corresponding .network file has the
  address with different prefix length, then the prefix length specified
  in the .network file will not be applied,
- we cannot specify multiple IPv4 addresses with different prefix
  length, e.g.
  ```
  Address=10.10.10.10/24
  Address=10.10.10.10/16
  ```
  This is spurious setup, but the kernel allows it.

Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/22515.

author: abellina
body:
Fixes https://github.com/rapidsai/cudf/issues/10333.

The repro case in the issue showed an illegal access error where the `output_index` of the strided loop in `fused_concatenate_kernel` can overflow for a large number of rows. 

For example, given 5 tables of exactly 250M rows each we would expect a result with 1,250,000,000 rows. 

The kernel is launched with 4,882,813 blocks (# of rows / 256 threads rounded up) with a stride of 1,250,000,128 (256 * 4,882,813). When `output_index` reaches 897,483,520, it overflows `output_index` on the first iteration.

The change below prevents the overflow by making `output_index` an `int64_t` and adds a test that shows that we can now concatenate up to `size_type::max - 1` rows.

body:
## Overview
All objects affected by gravity will suffer jittery near-holding behaviour because the "isKinematic" flag was incorrectly set to false when objects are held, causing gravity to "pull" the objects away from the hand, and the grip to resolve it, causing jitter. MRTK correctly returns the rigidbody back to it's original state when dropped again with this fix.

"isKinematic" is a flag for letting scripts take over movement of a rigidbody, which MRTK does in this case.

Both of these videos were taken in an oculus 2 device using the native record functionality. The low frame rate may make it hard to see, but there is a serious jitter in the first video that is remedied in the second using this fix.

![FixedMRTK](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9042770/155220555-c15df3bf-60c4-4d58-9bac-d27c1dbe8e3e.gif)

author: psasidhar
body:
Signed-off-by: Sasidhar Palaka <palakas@verizonmedia.com>

Main changes:

1) Added helper methods in Crypto.java and X509CertUtils to extract Subject DN, Subject CN, Issuer DN. The methods are designed to work with javax.servlet.request.X509Certificate attribute.

2) Modified ZTSImpl to send IssuerDN, SubjectDN, RSAModulusHash ONLY for register requests. This is deliberate so that the refresh requests can continue to come in with Athenz Service Identity Certificates and won't have any impact. This is done through a helper method, rather than adding another argument to generateInstanceConfirmObject, which already has many parameters.

3) SecureBoot provider looks at request certificate attributes (for CN and IssuerDN) only for register requests. And for refresh requests, the provider will look at certHostname filled in by ZTS.

4) AttrValidator interface and factory definitions.

author: katherineyevsukov
body:
## Description

This change is to update our DB tables to be more aligned with stakeholder vision. The "course types" table has been changed to a "programs" table, which now include the three types of programs our stakeholder actually offers. Columns have been added to classes table based on trello board checklist (name, min age, max age, etc.). I have also removed the open_seats_remaining column for normalization, as this is derived information we can gather from the enrollments table. The instructor approved course types table was switched to a programs instructors table. Also, this table is now using instructor id instead of profile id as many of the profile ids being used in the seeds did not belong to instructors. I have updated all references to old tables and seeds accordingly. The next step will be to update endpoints, middleware, and documentation to reflect these changes.

author: perryr16
body:
#### Any background context you want to provide?
When an unknown URL is entered a 404 error is initiated. SEED loads the sidebar, header, and 404 content. With the 404 page loaded the sidebar fails to lookup an active org and prompts the user to create a new one (similar to a user's first time visiting seed). Upon filling out a new organization, the user will be redirected to the home page where they will have a new organization attached to their profile.

#### What's this PR do?
Instead of sending users to a 404 or 500 page, all 404 and 500 errors will redirect to the home page '/' with an alert message in the header area indicating the error and reason.

The backend will redirect to '/' with a query param `?http_error=404` or `500`. The query parameter is visible in the url bar initially but soon disappears as the home page continues to load.

#### How should this be manually tested?
To test locally in docker a few settings need to be modified. 
- /config/settings/docker_dev.py --> change `DEBUG` to `False` 
- /docker-compose.dev.yml --> change `web`...`command:` to  `python3 manage.py runserver --insecure --settings=config.settings.docker_dev 0.0.0.0:80`

Go to any page that does not exist. You should be redirected to "/app/"

body:

Thank you for sharing your work and for opening a PR.

(!) IMPORTANT (!):
First make sure that you point your PR to the `devel` branch!

Now please read the comments carefully and try to provide information
on all relevant titles.

#########################################################################
-->

## Fixes #574 

<!--
Add the related issue in the form of #issue-number (Example #100)
-->

## New Behavior

Tweak the filtering parameters when filtering on VLAN groups. 
Previously you could define a VLAN an associate it to a VLAN group by doing this:

```
netbox_vlan:
  data:
    vid: 10
    name: VLAN 10
    vlan_group: My VLAN Group
```

It would do a call to `/api/vlan-groups/?slug=my-vlan-group`. This did not work when you have multiple VLANs with the same slug. So you'd try:

```
netbox_vlan:
  data:
    vid: 10
    name: VLAN 10
    vlan_group: 
      slug: My VLAN Group
      site: Site No 3
```

And this would do a call to `/api/vlan-groups/?slug=my-vlan-group&site_id=11`. But the VLAN group filtering is using `?site=11` to filter, so this would again return multiple results. To remediate this we now check if we're filtering a VLAN group, and if we are, we omit the `_id` on the query parameter. 

In addition, I have added `name` as a valid query parameter.

* api-change:``transfer``: Properties for Transfer Family used with SFTP, FTP, and FTPS protocols. Display Banners are bodies of text that can be displayed before and/or after a user authenticates onto a server using one of the previously mentioned protocols.
* api-change:``gamelift``: Increase string list limit from 10 to 100.
* api-change:``budgets``: This change introduces DescribeBudgetNotificationsForAccount API which returns budget notifications for the specified account
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.24.2
   ```
   ======

* api-change:``iam``: Documentation updates for AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).
* api-change:``redshift``: SDK release for Cross region datasharing and cost-control for cross region datasharing
* api-change:``evidently``: Add support for filtering list of experiments and launches by status
* api-change:``backup``: AWS Backup add new S3_BACKUP_OBJECT_FAILED and S3_RESTORE_OBJECT_FAILED event types in BackupVaultNotifications events list.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.24.1
   ```
   ======

* api-change:``ec2``: Documentation updates for EC2.
* api-change:``budgets``: Adds support for auto-adjusting budgets, a new budget method alongside fixed and planned. Auto-adjusting budgets introduces new metadata to configure a budget limit baseline using a historical lookback average or current period forecast.
* api-change:``ce``: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection now supports SNS FIFO topic subscribers.
* api-change:``glue``: Support for optimistic locking in UpdateTable
* api-change:``ssm``: Assorted ticket fixes and updates for AWS Systems Manager.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.24.0
   ```
   ======

* api-change:``appflow``: Launching Amazon AppFlow SAP as a destination connector SDK.
* feature:Parser: Adding support for parsing int/long types in rest-json response headers.
* api-change:``rds``: Adds support for determining which Aurora PostgreSQL versions support Babelfish.
* api-change:``athena``: This release adds a subfield, ErrorType, to the AthenaError response object in the GetQueryExecution API when a query fails.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.23.54
   ```
   =======

* api-change:``ssm``: Documentation updates for AWS Systems Manager.

   ```
   ### 1.23.53
   ```
   =======

* api-change:``cloudformation``: This SDK release adds AWS CloudFormation Hooks HandlerErrorCodes
* api-change:``lookoutvision``: This release makes CompilerOptions in Lookout for Vision's StartModelPackagingJob's Configuration object optional.
* api-change:``pinpoint``: This SDK release adds a new paramater creation date for GetApp and GetApps Api call
* api-change:``sns``: Customer requested typo fix in API documentation.
* api-change:``wafv2``: Adds support for AWS WAF Fraud Control account takeover prevention (ATP), with configuration options for the new managed rule group AWSManagedRulesATPRuleSet and support for application integration SDKs for Android and iOS mobile apps.

* api-change:``apprunner``: This release adds support for App Runner to route outbound network traffic of a service through an Amazon VPC. New API: CreateVpcConnector, DescribeVpcConnector, ListVpcConnectors, and DeleteVpcConnector. Updated API: CreateService, DescribeService, and UpdateService.
* api-change:``s3control``: This release adds support for S3 Batch Replication. Batch Replication lets you replicate existing objects, already replicated objects to new destinations, and objects that previously failed to replicate. Customers will receive object-level visibility of progress and a detailed completion report.
* api-change:``sagemaker``: Autopilot now generates an additional report with information on the performance of the best model, such as a Confusion matrix and  Area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUC-ROC). The path to the report can be found in CandidateArtifactLocations.
